purpose: Defines frame-rate-relative constants for video annotation. The module stores a base-30 reference table and provides functions to scale all timing constants to a video's actual frame rate exactly once, plus validation to confirm the video uses constant (not variable) frame rate.

public_api.name: BASE_FPS
public_api.role: Module constant (30.0). The reference frame rate used as the scaling denominator.

public_api.name: REST_SPEED_BASE30
public_api.role: Module constant (0.002). Base-30 per-frame speed multiplier for rest state animation.

public_api.name: START_SPEED_BASE30
public_api.role: Module constant (0.015). Base-30 per-frame speed multiplier for start state animation.

public_api.name: FpsConstants
public_api.role: Frozen dataclass containing fps-scaled timing parameters (rest_speed, windows, frame counts, etc.). Callers retrieve a single instance per video after calling scale_for_fps().

public_api.name: scale_for_fps(fps, overrides_base30)
public_api.role: Scales the base-30 table to a specific frame rate and returns a FpsConstants instance. Callers use this to convert all shipped constants from 30fps to the video's actual frame rate.

public_api.name: probe_fps(video_path)
public_api.role: Extracts the frame rate from a video file using ffprobe and validates it is constant (not variable). Callers use this to safely obtain the fps value before calling scale_for_fps().

stumbles.why_unclear: The code uses Fraction as an intermediate to convert frame-rate strings to floats. This handles rational notation like '30000/1001' (NTSC), but the comment does not explain why Fraction is necessary instead of parsing directly as float.
